user.title: Govee LAN Segments
user.description: Pick a light found on your network, or enter its IP address. LAN Control must be enabled for it in the Govee Home app.

manual.title: Govee LAN Segments
manual.description: Enter the light's IP address. LAN Control must be enabled for it in the Govee Home app. Supported models: {models}.

reconfigure.title: Change IP address
reconfigure.description: Enter the light's new IP address.

error.invalid_host: Enter an IP address, such as 192.168.1.50.
error.cannot_connect: No reply from that address. Check the IP, that the light is powered, and that LAN Control is on in the Govee Home app.
error.unsupported: That device answered, but its model isn't supported yet.
error.port_in_use: UDP port 4002 is already in use on this Home Assistant host, usually by the Govee lights local integration. Remove it and try again.

abort.already_configured: This device is already set up.
abort.port_in_use: UDP port 4002 is already in use on this Home Assistant host, usually by the Govee lights local integration. Remove it and try again.
abort.wrong_device: That IP address belongs to a different Govee device.

port_conflict_govee_light_local.title: Govee lights local is blocking Govee LAN Segments
port_conflict_govee_light_local.description:
Govee devices send every reply to UDP port 4002, so only one Govee LAN integration can run on a Home Assistant host. The Govee lights local integration currently holds the port ({error}).

Govee LAN Segments replaces it for supported lights. Remove Govee lights local under **Settings > Devices & services**, then restart Home Assistant.

port_conflict.title: Govee LAN Segments can't open UDP port 4002
port_conflict.description: Govee devices send every reply to UDP port 4002, and something else on this Home Assistant host is using it ({error}). Stop whatever holds the port (often another Govee integration or add-on), then restart Home Assistant.
